project.name: Regulation 28
project.graph_query: Which files implement the human wiki, LLM wiki, evidence governance, source register, evidence matrix, validation queue, design contract, Graphify publication, verification, dependency management, local service, and deployment?

formal_conformance.reason: The project has no .wiki-standard.yaml and deliberately claims only a legacy Level 4 position. Results below infer reusable capabilities without upgrading that claim or creating a waiver.

profile_assessment.declared_legacy_profile: Level 4 Graph-Linked; no Level 5 or Level 6 claim
profile_assessment.summary: The most mature generated analytical and bounded Ask implementation in the sample. Its legacy level label understates current operational evidence but correctly refuses OKF and full-release claims.

limitations: Graphify and browser-verification tooling are not fully pinned as repository dependencies.

candidate_false_positive_risks.finding: The presence of advanced runtime and browser evidence must not silently promote the project's explicit Level 4 legacy claim.
2D/3D presence and pinned CDN URLs do not prove repository-local runtime conformance.
A verify script name alone does not prove a non-mutating check; its graph:update step must be classified.

candidate_false_negative_risks.finding: The strongest canonical evidence lives in CSV with generated Markdown views; a Markdown-only role detector would invert authority.
The legacy Level 4 label understates generated analysis, Ask, service and deployment maturity; capabilities must remain independent from a single level.
LLM and evidence controls span AGENTS.md, canonical CSVs, generated views and maintenance pages.

recommendations: Add a candidate manifest mapping canonical CSV inputs separately from generated Markdown views; preserve the explicit legacy claim until adoption is chosen.
Implement a non-destructive OKF v0.2 sidecar over canonical concepts and records with round-trip tests.
Vendor graph runtimes and add a no-network browser check; keep the analytical map distinct from the technical Graphify graph.
Complete security/source-retention/copyright/licensing policy mappings and add CI if this moves toward managed-full.
Define a standard-upgrade patch workflow that never overwrites the generated analytical model or Ask security controls.
audit_limitations: The audit included two pre-existing dirty working-tree entries.
Graphify query output was routing evidence only and had poor recall for the full analytical architecture.
Historical browser, Ask and deployment records were inspected but not replayed.
No external production URL or live Ask inference was invoked.
